frameworks.name: Free-to-Paid Conversion Mechanisms
frameworks.definition: Three structured pathways to convert free community members into paid offerings: onboarding sales calls, self-serve course progression through a video sales letter structure, and recurring group calls with soft CTAs.

claims.text: When paid-media ads initially work then stop working without price changes, the constraint is usually audience depletion rather than offer rejection. As Facebook ads progress from warm audiences (people who know the brand) through one-degree-removed connections to cold audiences, conversion rates decline because cold audiences lack pre-existing trust.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: As the warm audience (known to the brand) is exhausted, the algorithm expands to one-degree-removed connections who lack pre-existing familiarity, reducing conversion.
bounded_by: Does not apply when offer or creative fundamentally changes

claims.text: Community businesses that rely exclusively on paid acquisition experience rapid audience depletion. The highest-performing segment builds parallel free and paid community models: the free tier feeds the paid tier, creating a two-community acquisition strategy.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Free communities convert easily and serve as a source of warm leads for paid offerings, reducing dependence on cold paid acquisition.

claims.text: A benchmark for free-community sign-up rate is 20% of total clicks. At this rate, cost per new member is calculated as cost per click multiplied by five.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: paid traffic acquisition to free offer

claims.text: Of free community members who are manually worked as leads, approximately 10% convert to paid offerings, providing a baseline for revenue modeling.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: The most effective free-to-paid conversion pathway uses the video sales letter format: an origin story establishing the opportunity, three case studies representing different obstacles (self, others, circumstances), and a clear call-to-action. This five-piece structure mirrors a webinar sales architecture.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: The origin story contextualizes the problem; three diverse case studies demonstrate solution applicability across different scenarios; the CTA creates a clear conversion moment.

claims.text: Weekly group calls into a free community where value is delivered and problems are solved, followed by a soft CTA for paid offerings, generate ongoing conversion without aggressive selling. This recurring cadence produces a steady stream of new paid members and typically fills multiple spots per week.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Solving problems on the call builds perceived value and authority; the soft CTA becomes natural after delivering results.

claims.text: Direct messaging to new free community members for one-on-one relationship building (without immediate sales solicitation) creates authentic dialogue that increases paid conversion. The approach prioritizes relationship depth before monetization.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Authentic dialogue and relationship building reduce perceived sales pressure, increasing willingness to engage.

claims.text: A free-to-paid community model is viable if paid community pricing multiplied by 10 is less than or equal to the price of the free community offer, because the paid monthly revenue from conversion must exceed acquisition costs from the first payment onward.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: If the paid tier price × 10 exceeds free-offer costs, acquisition becomes unprofitable.

examples.text: A paid school community with advanced content for larger business owners can be presented to free community members as a natural next step. In a weekly call with 100+ free members, mentioning the advanced paid tier will typically result in some members immediately requesting access.

When Jesus Hernandez increased his community business price and ads stopped converting, the issue was not the price change itself (he decreased price and ads still underperformed), but rather his warm audience pool was exhausted, leaving only cold prospects from one-degree-removed connections who were less likely to convert.

practices.text: Implement three parallel conversion mechanisms within the free community: onboarding calls, a five-module self-serve video course, and weekly group calls.
Manually work free community members as leads before automating follow-up sequences, especially in early-stage community businesses.
Structure free-community courses as video sales letters with origin story, three case studies, and clear CTA rather than generic educational content.
When paid-media results decline, diagnose whether the constraint is audience pool depletion (widen to cold outreach or build free community) versus offer/creative issues before pivoting pricing.
